description:
Switch the development locus from /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox (private
clone) to ~/Developer/benchbox-public (public clone). Archive
joeharris76/benchbox-private on GitHub. No GitHub-side rename, no
visibility flip — under Option B the existing public repo
(joeharris76/BenchBox) stays canonical with its URL unchanged.

Pre-conditions:
- Phase 4 succeeded: v0.3.0 on PyPI, _project/** history visible on public
  via filter-merge
- All in-flight work on private branches has been merged to private main
  and synced to public via the curated flow (or cherry-picked manually
  onto public branches)
- Local mirror backup of benchbox-private exists

Most steps are reversible. The only step worth pausing for is GitHub-side
archival of benchbox-private (reversible via "unarchive", but worth
thinking once).

Plan file: /Users/joe/.claude/plans/single-repo-migration.md (Phase 5).

anti_patterns.dont: change the canonical repo URL or rename joeharris76/BenchBox
anti_patterns.why: that triggers an irreversible visibility-event chain that Option B specifically avoided (vs. Option A which did rename).

anti_patterns.dont: delete benchbox-private from GitHub at the end of this phase
anti_patterns.why: external links, forks, and stars (if any) point to it; archiving preserves them with read-only access. Deletion is Phase 9 (optional).

anti_patterns.dont: delete the renamed local clone (BenchBox.retired-YYYYMMDD/) at the end of this phase
anti_patterns.why: it is the ultimate "did I lose any in-flight work" reference for 60+ days.

anti_patterns.dont: enable branch-protection's linear-history rule before Phase 4 w6 lands
anti_patterns.why: that merge commit is a non-linear one-time event; the rule applies from-this-point-forward, not retroactively.

anti_patterns.dont: push commits to public main from the retired private clone after w5
anti_patterns.why: the retired clone has stale knowledge of public's history (curated mirror, before the migration commits) and any push from there would create divergent history. Only push from ~/Developer/benchbox-public going forward.

preserves.behavior: All git history on joeharris76/BenchBox is preserved untouched (no rewrites, no force-pushes).
All git history on joeharris76/benchbox-private is preserved (archive is read-only but full history accessible).
PyPI wheels for previously-published versions remain installable (PyPI is independent of repo state).
The _project/** filter-merge from Phase 4 remains intact (the merge commit and its preserved sub-commits).
The mirror backup from w1 is retained for at least 90 days as the ultimate fallback.

verifications.description: Private repo is archived on GitHub
Public repo URL unchanged and accessible
Retired private clone exists at expected path

verifications.command: cd ~/Developer/benchbox-public && uv run -- python -m pytest -m fast --collect-only -q | tail -1
verifications.expected: non-zero test count, no collection errors

verifications.description: CLAUDE.md no longer mentions the two-remote rule (after w9 merges)

work_units.notes:
git clone --mirror git@github.com:joeharris76/benchbox-private.git \
  /tmp/benchbox-private-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).git
Verify the clone size matches GitHub's reported repo size. Keep
this backup until at least Phase 8 ships green and 60-day soak passes.
work_units.summary: Create local mirror backup of benchbox-private before archival

work_units.notes:
Brief note for any external visitors:
  "BenchBox absorbed development from a private fork on YYYY-MM-DD.
  _project/** retains the original commit history; other paths
  arrived as a single squashed migration commit. The previous
  private repo (joeharris76/benchbox-private) has been archived."
Remove in Phase 9.
work_units.summary: (Optional) Pin a MIGRATION-NOTES.md at repo root for 60-90 days

work_units.notes:
cd ~/Developer/benchbox-public
git status                     # must be clean
git log -1 --oneline           # confirm v0.3.0 release commit present
git log --oneline -- _project/TODO/ | head -3  # confirm filter-merge worked

cd /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox
git status                     # must be clean
git branch -a                  # review feature branches
git stash list                 # nothing important stashed
# For each non-merged feature branch on private:
#   - merge to private main and sync via curated flow, OR
#   - cherry-pick onto a public branch via gh
Stop here if anything is dirty or unmerged.
work_units.summary: Confirm pre-conditions: clean public clone, no in-flight private branches with valuable work

work_units.notes:
cd ~/Developer/benchbox-public
uv sync     # set up venv if not already
uv run -- python -m pytest -m fast
uv run ruff check .
uv run ty check
# All green. If any test or lint fails: it is the responsibility of
# the migration to fix before retiring the private clone — once
# retired, you are in single-repo mode.
work_units.summary: Verify the public clone is fully functional as the new dev locus

work_units.notes:
GitHub UI: Settings on joeharris76/benchbox-private -> Danger zone ->
"Archive this repository". Confirm.
The repo becomes read-only. Existing collaborators (just you) lose
write access. URL still resolves; clones still work.
Reversible via "Unarchive" if needed.

mv /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox \
   /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox.retired-$(date +%Y%m%d)
The retired path remains as a reference for 60+ days. Renaming
prevents shell muscle-memory from accidentally `cd`-ing into it
and committing/pushing somewhere stale.
work_units.summary: Retire the local private clone (rename, do not delete)

work_units.notes:
Two options — pick whichever:
- mv ~/Developer/benchbox-public /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox
  (rename the public clone to the canonical path)
- ln -s ~/Developer/benchbox-public /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox
  (symlink — existing IDE/shell sessions keep working)
Or do nothing — keep the public clone at ~/Developer/benchbox-public
and update muscle memory.
work_units.summary: (Optional) Reclaim /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox path for the public clone

work_units.notes:
GitHub UI: Settings -> Branches -> Add rule for main:
  - Require pull request before merging
  - Require status checks: select the CI workflow from Phase 2
  - Require linear history    [add ONLY AFTER Phase 4 w6 merge commit lands]
  - Allow squash-merge ONLY (uncheck merge commits and rebase-merge
    in repo Settings -> General)
  - Block force pushes
  - Block deletions
Do NOT require approving review (solo maintainer would self-block).
Test by opening a no-op PR and squash-merging it.

Note: the linear-history rule conflicts with the Phase 4 _project/**
filter-merge commit. That merge is a one-time exception; enable
linear-history AFTER it has landed and from this point forward all
subsequent merges are squash-only.
work_units.summary: Set up branch protection on joeharris76/BenchBox main

work_units.notes:
PyPI Homepage already points at https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox,
which is unchanged under Option B (no rename happened). Verify by
visiting https://pypi.org/project/benchbox/ and checking the Homepage
link resolves.
Update only if it currently points elsewhere or if other URL fields
(issues, source) need correction.
work_units.summary: Verify PyPI project URLs (no change needed under Option B)

work_units.notes:
Open a PR on public to remove the "Git Remotes - CRITICAL" section
in CLAUDE.md and the equivalent in AGENTS.md so future sessions
stop pushing to the wrong (now non-existent) remote. Replace with a
one-line placeholder:
  "Single repo, single origin (joeharris76/BenchBox).
  See docs/operations/release-guide.md."
The rest of the docs cleanup is Phase 7. This step is the minimum
to prevent foot-guns in subsequent commits.
work_units.summary: Strip two-remote-rule sections from CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md (interim - full update in Phase 7)
